about.title: About This Site
about.subtitle: You want to see China. The Chinese internet won't let you in. I went in for you.
about.brandStory: The name nods to Liu Cixin's short story 'With Her Eyes' (带上她的眼睛), by the author of The Three-Body Problem — a traveler carries a borrowed pair of eyes so that someone far away can see the world. We changed one word: these are MY eyes. Every vlog, guide and photo on this site is something I have watched, read and judged myself — a hundred pairs of local eyes, lent to you for your trip, to see the China that English search engines never reach.
about.missionTitle: For Those Who Can't See It Yet
about.offerSubtitle: No algorithm. Everything picked by a human.
about.ctaTitle: Borrow a Pair of Eyes First?
about.ctaSubtitle: See the real China through the screen — and when you finally make it here, the roads will still be there.
about.missionP1: Every day, thousands of people Google "China travel" and get the same decade-old guidebooks and the same sponsored lists. Meanwhile, the China that's actually alive is on the other side of a wall: a Finnish family eating 15 Sichuan meals in three days, a guy riding local buses from Beijing to Shanghai, first-person POV of a cliff plank walk on Mount Hua. It's all right there. You just can't search it, and you can't read it.
about.missionP2: Just like the girl trapped at the center of the Earth in the story — it's not that she didn't want to see. She couldn't get out. Wanting to see a place, blocked by layers of language and platforms: that's the exact ache this site exists to relieve.
about.missionP3: So this site does one simple thing: I drill a small hole through that wall for you. Every vlog, every guide here is something I watched first, judged, and decided was worth your time. Not an algorithm — me. And if you can't make the trip just yet, that's fine. Borrow the eyes first. See it from where you are.
